clue.text: Listener's choice: retro piece for singer and woodwind

indicators.note: a listener hears the word, so what follows is a sound, not a spelling

parts.note: a choice is a pick

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the word for a singer's piece runs right to left

parts.note: a piece for one singer is a solo

explanation.surface: A radio listener requests an old-fashioned number for a vocalist backed by woodwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' turns SOLO into OLOS; the sound of 'pick' is spelt PICC here.
explanation.definitionFit: Small flutes are members of the woodwind family, so the plural names several such instruments.

clue.text: Departs before noon after stay's over in German city

indicators.note: after means the turned word comes first and the departure piece follows it
over means the word for stay is turned backwards in this down clue

parts.note: to stay is to stop; the 's is a link here
d is the timetable abbreviation for departs
am, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A train leaves in the morning after a stopover in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam is the capital of Brandenburg, near Berlin, a German urban centre.

clue.text: Officer keeping gold in chest

indicators.note: keeping means the chest holds the gold inside

parts.note: a commode is a chest of drawers
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A naval man keeps his gold locked in a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A commodore is a senior naval officer ranking above captain.

clue.text: Biscuit a cook half-heartedly prepared with tea

indicators.note: prepared means the letters are made into something new
half-heartedly means one of the two middle letters of cook is lost

explanation.surface: A cook makes biscuits without much enthusiasm, served with tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' leaves COK; with A and TEA, 'prepared' rearranges ACOKTEA.
explanation.definitionFit: An oatcake is a savoury Scottish cracker made of oatmeal.

clue.text: Use tool for repairing part of shoe

indicators.note: repairing means the letters are mended into a new shape

explanation.surface: A cobbler is told to use a particular tool to mend a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The outsole is the bottom layer of a shoe that touches the ground.

clue.text: Endless old Roman road in the country

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for old is dropped

parts.note: old can mean late, as in the late king
via is Latin for road, as in Via Appia

explanation.surface: A traveller follows the remains of an ancient Roman road through the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' acts on the word for old, which here means former, as in 'the late king'; 'in the' is only link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia is a Baltic state, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Painting wins top prize in the end

parts.note: lands means wins, as in lands a contract
a cap is a top or lid

indicators.note: in the end means the last letter of prize is taken

explanation.surface: A painting finally carries off the top award at an art contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of scenery is a landscape, a genre of picture.

clue.text: Outburst of anger over a painting

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: a temper is a fit of rage

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage about a painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made with egg yolk, and a picture done in that medium.

clue.text: Drive up motorway, heading north to place of learning

indicators.note: to means the next piece is joined on after
heading north in a down clue means the words up and motorway are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, with the 1 read as I
LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A driver heads up the motorway towards a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading north' turns UPMI into IMPU; the M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive as a noun means an urge or motivating force, the same as a sudden urge.

clue.text: Times includes worthless stuff about seduction

indicators.note: includes means the word for times holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: tempi is a plural of tempo, musical time
tat is cheap worthless goods
on can mean about, concerning

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs trashy material on the subject of seduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper but means musical tempos in the plural; 'includes' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Seduction is enticement to do wrong, the same idea as luring someone astray.

clue.text: Blue hair? The ultimate in wacky

parts.note: a mop is a thick mass of hair

indicators.note: the ultimate in means the final letter of wacky is taken

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether dyed blue hair is the last word in eccentric style.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue here means low-spirited and dejected, an adjective matching gloomy and listless.

clue.text: Wanting to jilt attractive female, announce the bad news

parts.note: to drop a partner is to jilt them
a bombshell is a strikingly attractive woman

explanation.surface: A man wants to dump his glamorous girlfriend and tell everyone the sad story.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to reveal shocking or unwelcome information suddenly.

clue.text: When apes first appear and come in playing to rear of cage

indicators.note: playing means the letters of come in are performed in a new order
rear of means the last letter of cage is added at the back

explanation.surface: A zoo-like scene where apes emerge and come in to play at the back of their cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' signals the anagram of COMEIN; 'apes' is part of the definition, the geological epoch, not the surface's zoo animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The epoch of about 23 to 5 million years ago is when apes are first found in fossils.

clue.text: Quality of a fruitcake, in more ways than one

definitions.text: Quality of a fruitcake, in more ways than one

parts.words: Quality of a fruitcake, in more ways than one
parts.note: a fruitcake is a crazy person, and also a cake full of nuts, so both readings describe the same quality

explanation.surface: Describing a characteristic of a slightly mad person, with a nod to baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Craziness is the trait of a fruitcake person, and a cake packed with nuts has it literally.

clue.text: Soldier's preferred form of defence

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
pet means favourite, preferred

explanation.surface: A soldier names his favourite way to defend himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A low protective wall on a fortification or roof shields defenders, a type of defensive work.

clue.text: Inferior writer of poor operettas

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of operettas are badly put together and rearranged

explanation.surface: A second-rate author is blamed for some feeble light operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetaster is a writer of trashy verse, a bad poet.

clue.text: Birds going about in pants

indicators.note: going about means the birds surround the next piece

parts.note: tits are small songbirds
in meaning fashionable is hep, an old form of hip

explanation.surface: Birds are flying around inside someone's underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang for rubbish, not trousers or underwear; HEP is old slang for trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang pants means awful, and the phrase means the very worst.

clue.text: Where danger lurks, son gets in a stew

indicators.note: gets in means the son goes inside the stew

parts.note: hotpot is a Lancashire stew of meat under sliced potato

explanation.surface: A boy finds himself in trouble, a dangerous situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spot is a place of conflict or peril, idiom for a danger zone.

clue.text: Stop a press conference?

parts.note: PR, public relations, deals with the press
a conference is an event

explanation.surface: A call to halt a press briefing.
explanation.walkthrough: A press conference is a PR event, read cryptically.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it happening.

clue.text: Musicians producing singular record recalling Let It Be

parts.note: s is the grammar abbreviation for singular
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: recalling means calling back, so the proof-reader's word is read backwards

parts.note: stet is the proof-reader's instruction meaning let it stand

explanation.surface: A band produces a solo record that harks back to the Beatles' Let It Be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let It Be' looks like the Beatles song but is the proof-reader's instruction; 'recalling' signals the backward reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of seven performers are bands of musicians, each a set number of players.

clue.text: Team's excited after recruiting ace new scorer

indicators.note: recruiting means the stirred letters take in the next pieces
excited means the letters of team's are stirred up

parts.note: team's read as team is gives the letters of team plus s
a is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: A team gets excited after signing a top new goalscorer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' is a composer, not a goalscorer: Smetana wrote The Bartered Bride. 'excited' gives SMETA, AN goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scorer writes musical scores; Smetana was a Czech composer.

clue.text: A school friend comes round for Easter

indicators.note: comes round means the friend surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend from school visits for the Easter holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Paschal means relating to the Passover or the Christian resurrection festival.

clue.text: Superficial, like a very short play?

definitions.meaning: a sketch is a short comic play, so adding y makes like one

explanation.definitionFit: Sketchy means slight and lacking detail, and playfully means resembling a comic skit.

clue.text: Theatre in West London initially adapted play

indicators.note: adapted means the letters are reworked into a new form, like a script
initially means the first letter of London is taken

explanation.surface: A West London theatre puts on an adaptation of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: The Winter's Tale is a Shakespeare drama, an example of a stage work.

clue.text: People get cut in odd places. by this?

definitions.text: People get cut in odd places. by this?

indicators.note: cutting the letters in odd positions leaves the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Fencers get nicked in unexpected parts of the body by a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of PEOPLEGET to leave the even ones; the result is a weapon that does exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencing sword can cut opponents, so the whole clue describes the blade.

clue.text: Understanding way medicine should be swallowed? Quite the opposite

indicators.text: should be swallowed? Quite the opposite
indicators.note: the surface says the medicine is swallowed by the way; the opposite means the medicine swallows the way

parts.note: an emetic is a medicine that induces vomiting
a path is a way

explanation.surface: Advice on how a sick person ought to take their pills, then a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: an emetic makes you bring things up, the opposite of swallowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Able to share others' feelings is the sense of sympathetic, understanding.

clue.text: Facts and figures about university ranking

indicators.note: about means the facts surround the next letter

parts.note: stats is short for statistics, facts and figures

explanation.surface: Data on a university's standing in league tables.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is standing or rank within a social or professional order.

clue.text: Like one going by boat and then railway without bother

indicators.note: without means outside, so the pieces surround the bother

parts.note: so means and then, as in so off we went
ail means to trouble or bother

explanation.surface: A traveller goes by ship and then train, without any hassle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside puts AIL in SO+RLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailorly means seamanlike, befitting a mariner.
